answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to lock a refundable stake that only matures after sustained honest work — like a lantern that must burn a full season before it pays light. Reputation then grows slowly from verified deliveries, the way a yarrow root spreads underground, not from self-declared claims. An attacker spinning up thousands of ivory-clean sock puppets must fund every stake and wait out the same slow maturation, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes plus months of idle capital — far more than any single fake deal could ever earn.
